target_moa.text: Nitrofuran antiprotozoal; mechanism not fully understood — nifurtimox is activated by Type I and Type II nitroreductases to toxic intermediate metabolites and/or reactive oxygen species that induce DNA damage and cell death of T. cruzi.

citations.quote: The mechanism of action of nifurtimox is not fully understood. Studies suggest that nifurtimox is metabolized/activated, by Type I (oxygen insensitive) and Type II (oxygen sensitive) nitroreductases (NTR) leading to production of toxic intermediate metabolites and/or reactive oxygen species that induce DNA damage and cell death of both intracellular and extracellular forms of *T. cruzi*.
The mechanism of action of nifurtimox, a nitroheterocyclic molecule, is not fully understood.

key_safety.text: Most frequently reported adverse reactions in the 60-day arm: vomiting (14.6%), abdominal pain (13.2%), headache (12.8%), decreased appetite (10.5%), nausea (8.2%), pyrexia (7.3%), rash (5.5%). Discontinuation due to adverse reactions in 14 of 330 (4.2%) patients. Serious hypersensitivity reactions include DRESS and anaphylaxis; animal studies indicate risk for embryo-fetal toxicity.

citations.quote: The most frequently reported adverse reactions in patients treated with LAMPIT for 60 days were vomiting (14.6%), abdominal pain (13.2%), headache (12.8%), decreased appetite (10.5%), nausea (8.2%), pyrexia (7.3%), rash (5.5%).
Discontinuation of LAMPIT due to adverse reactions occurred in 14 of 330 (4.2%) patients overall
Hypersensitivity reactions include rash, urticaria, DRESS, eosinophilia, and anaphylaxis.
Animal studies indicate a risk for embryo-fetal toxicity.

requirement.text: Conduct a worldwide descriptive study collecting prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to LAMPIT during pregnancy to assess pregnancy/maternal complications and effects on fetus, neonate, and infant, over a minimum of 10 years.

citations.quote: 3868-2 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to LAMPIT (nifurtimox) during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The study will collect information for a minimum of 10 years.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Number of treated patients who became IgG antibody negative or showed an at least 20% decrease in optical density on two different IgG antibody tests against T. cruzi antigens (change in serologic test results).

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on the number of treated patients who became immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody negative or who showed an at least 20% decrease in optical density on two different IgG antibody tests against antigens of *T. cruzi*.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Continue to follow subjects in Study 16027 (CHICO SECURE) for an additional 3 years as a required confirmatory study to confirm that a 20% decrease in optical density at 1 year post-treatment predicts seroconversion at 4 years post-treatment.

citations.quote: The Applicant will continue to follow the subjects in Study 16027 for an additional 3 years as a required confirmatory study for the Subpart H approval. The follow up study will provide confirmation that the 20% decrease in optical density at 1 year post-treatment in children from 8 months to less than 18 years old is predictive of seroconversion at 4 years post-treatment.

summary.text: NDA 213464 (a 505(b)(2) application) for nifurtimox was submitted December 6, 2019 and received priority review. Nifurtimox had orphan drug designation for Chagas disease. It was approved under accelerated approval (21 CFR 314.500) based on a surrogate serologic endpoint, with a required Subpart H confirmatory follow-up of Study 16027 to verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: Bayer submitted NDA 213464 for Lampit (nifurtimox) tablets, 30 mg and 120 mg on December 6, 2019, for the treatment of Chagas disease. This submission included a request for priority review and for consideration for a Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher (TDPRV) upon approval.
It is approved under the provisions of accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 314.500), effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling.
The Applicant will continue to follow the subjects in Study 16027 for an additional 3 years as a required confirmatory study for the Subpart H approval.

description.text: Converted accelerated approval to full approval for pediatric patients (birth to <18 years, ≥2.5 kg) with Chagas disease

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application proposes conversion of Lampit from accelerated approval to full approval for use in pediatric patients (birth to less than 18 years of age and weighing at least 2.5 kg) for the treatment of Chagas disease (American Trypanosomiasis), caused by *Trypanosoma cruzi*. Specifically, the following sections of the prescribing information have been revised: **HIGHLIGHTS OF PRESCRIBING INFORMATION, INDICATIONS AND USAGE (1), USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS (8) and CLINICAL STUDIES (14), and a REFERENCES (15)** section has been added. Additionally, minor revisions to the **PATIENT INFORMATION** have been included.
